notes: Model-agnostic prompt blocks. Placeholders use {{name}}. The tools render these into the generated deliverables so a writer or a downstream agent can paste them into any model.

roles.showrunner: You are a narrative showrunner: you protect the premise, the thematic question, and the reader promise across every deliverable.
roles.outline: You are a story architect: you build causal spines where every beat is caused by the previous choice and forces the next.
roles.scene: You are a scene writer: you write scenes built on want, obstacle, tactic, and turn, and you cut anything that does not cost someone something.
roles.character: You are a character designer: you build people who want two incompatible things and reveal it through action under pressure.
roles.diagnostic: You are a story diagnostician: you name problems in causal, testable terms, cite the evidence, and propose the smallest fix.
roles.ethics: You are a rights and representation reviewer: you flag real-person risk, stereotype, cultural extraction, and unlabelled invention.

brief_questions.title: Brief interview
brief_questions.body: Ask these in one pass and record answers verbatim: 1) What must the audience feel by the end? 2) Which format, length, and platform, and what is the hard budget? 3) Who is the audience and what must never appear on the page? 4) Which themes are you testing, and which answer must the story refuse? 5) What are your non-negotiables (canon, cast, setting, deliverable dates)? 6) What existing works should this be unmistakably not like?

premise_core.title: Premise core

premise_angle.title: Premise angle {{index}}
premise_angle.body: Generate premise direction {{index}} using the {{angle}} lens. Required: a different protagonist role, a different world rule, and a different structural risk from angle {{previous}}. Produce: logline (<=40 words), opening image, central pressure, the lie the protagonist believes, and the cost of the climax. Flag any similarity to a known work and how this direction differs.

logline.title: Logline
logline.body: One sentence, {{format}} length budget: [protagonist with a specific want] must [action under pressure] or [concrete consequence], but [the obstacle that is also their flaw].

outline_beat.title: Beat {{beat_index}} - {{beat_name}} ({{position_percent}}%)

character_card.title: Character - {{name}}
character_card.body:
Role: {{role}} | Age: {{age}} | Function in the argument: {{function}}
Define: want (external, actionable), need (internal, resisted), wound (specific event), lie believed, competence, incompetence, speech pattern (with one sample line), habitual gesture, relationship debt, and the choice that will cost them most. Add one contradiction that the reader will notice before the character does.

scene_card.title: Scene {{number}} - {{title}}

comic_page.title: Page {{page}} - {{title}}

game_node.title: Node {{node_id}} - {{title}}

revision_pass.title: Revision pass - {{pass}}
revision_pass.body:
{{pass_instruction}}
Work at the level of {{level}}. For every issue found, return: location (section/scene/line), evidence (short quote or beat), the causal problem in one sentence, the smallest sufficient fix, and the risk of that fix. Order by severity: critical, high, medium, low. Do not rewrite stylistic preference as error.

continuity_report.title: Continuity audit
continuity_report.body: Check every claim in the bible against the manuscript: names, ages, dates, distances, travel time, injuries, possessions, knowledge states (who knows what, when), stated rules of magic/technology, promises made to the reader, and resolved/unresolved threads. Return one record per finding with: entity, field, bible value, manuscript value, first conflicting location, severity, and whether the bible or the manuscript should change.

audit_report.title: Manuscript audit
audit_report.body: Score each rubric dimension 1-5 with evidence. Name the two structural problems that, fixed, would raise the most dimensions. Give one paragraph of actionable direction. Do not praise generically; every comment must cite a location.

export_synopsis.title: Synopsis
export_synopsis.body: Write a {{word_budget}}-word synopsis in present tense that spoils the ending: setup, escalation, the irreversible choice, the climax cost, and the changed normal. No rhetorical questions, no theme statement in the final line.

export_treatment.title: Treatment
export_treatment.body: Write a {{word_budget}}-word treatment: premise, world rules that create pressure, principal cast with competing answers to the thematic question, act-by-act causal summary, visual or sonic motif plan, and the production constraints this treatment respects.

export_style_sheet.title: Style sheet
export_style_sheet.body: Define the prose contract: POV and distance, tense, sentence length distribution, permitted and forbidden constructions, dialogue punctuation, profanity and dialect policy, motif vocabulary, chapter or scene length targets, and three sample sentences that establish the register.

style_voices.label: Plain and concrete
style_voices.guidance: Short declaratives, concrete nouns, almost no adverbs, metaphor only when it replaces explanation.

style_voices.label: Lyrical
style_voices.guidance: Long rhythmic sentences alternating with short stops, image-forward, restrained abstraction.

style_voices.label: Noir
style_voices.guidance: First person past, clipped, sardonic, sensory detail as judgement, dialogue carrying subtext.

style_voices.label: Warm and comic
style_voices.guidance: Present-leaning, conversational rhythm, humour from character specificity, no punching down.

style_voices.label: Clinical and cool
style_voices.guidance: Neutral register, procedural detail, emotion carried by omission and precision.

style_voices.label: Epic
style_voices.guidance: Cadenced, formal register, long arcs of cause, elevated diction used sparingly against plain detail.

style_voices.label: Vernacular
style_voices.guidance: Regional syntax and rhythm, dialogue-forward, glossary-free clarity for outside readers.

revision_passes.label: Structural pass
revision_passes.instruction: Test the causal spine: does every act break close a door, does every beat pay a setup, is the climax the only possible consequence of the protagonist's flaw?

revision_passes.label: Scene pass
revision_passes.instruction: For each scene, state goal, obstacle, tactic, turn, and consequence. Mark scenes with no turn and scenes that repeat an earlier scene's function.

revision_passes.label: Character pass
revision_passes.instruction: Trace want, need, wound, and lie across scenes. Find where a character acts against their established logic without a stated cause.

revision_passes.label: Dialogue pass
revision_passes.instruction: Test speech distinctness with tags removed. Cut exposition disguised as dialogue. Convert statements of feeling into tactics.

revision_passes.label: Prose pass
revision_passes.instruction: Remove hedging, filter words, adverbial intensifiers, cliche, and abstraction stacks. Vary sentence length. Prefer concrete verbs.

revision_passes.label: Pacing pass
revision_passes.instruction: Compare tension targets to scene lengths. Compress low-pressure scenes, expand decision scenes, and place deliberate rests before the climax.

revision_passes.label: Continuity pass
revision_passes.instruction: Reconcile names, dates, distances, injuries, possessions, and knowledge states. Update the bible or the manuscript, never both silently.

revision_passes.label: Theme pass
revision_passes.instruction: Identify every statement of theme. Convert each into a test the character can fail. Ensure the antagonist holds the strongest opposing answer.

revision_passes.label: Rights and representation pass
revision_passes.instruction: Flag real persons, real protected groups, cultural extraction, stereotype, and unlabelled invention. Require a source or a change.

revision_passes.label: Format readiness pass
revision_passes.instruction: Check word or page budget, scene count, cast count, panel and bubble budget, node reachability, and platform limits. Report exact numbers.
